record.paper_title: Some open questions and conjectures about visibility and iteration in bounded convex domains in ℂ^N
record.original_question: For a bounded convex domain Ω ⊂ ℂ^N, call Ω complex visible if for every pair of distinct boundary points p,q ∈ ∂Ω there exists a compact set K ⊂⊂ Ω such that whenever z_k → p and w_k → q, every sequence of complex geodesics φ_k with z_k,w_k ∈ φ_k(𝔻) satisfies φ_k(𝔻) ∩ K ≠ ∅ for all sufficiently large k. Is this notion actually equivalent to ordinary visibility? In other words, is a bounded convex domain visible if and only if it is complex visible?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.9. Let Ω ⊂ C^N be a bounded convex domain. Then Ω is visible if and only if it is complex visible.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^N$ be a bounded convex domain, and let $\mathbb{D} \subset \mathbb{C}$ denote the open unit disk. A holomorphic map $\varphi: \mathbb{D} \to \Omega$ is called a complex geodesic if it is an isometry between the Poincaré distance on $\mathbb{D}$ and the Kobayashi distance on $\Omega$. The domain $\Omega$ is said to be visible if for every pair of distinct boundary points $p, q \in \partial \Omega$ there exists a compact set $K \subset\subset \Omega$ and neighborhoods $U_p, U_q$ of $p, q$ in $\overline{\Omega}$ such that every real Kobayashi geodesic in $\Omega$ joining a point of $U_p$ to a point of $U_q$ meets $K$.

Call $\Omega$ complex visible if for every pair of distinct boundary points $p, q \in \partial \Omega$ there exists a compact set $K \subset\subset \Omega$ such that whenever sequences $z_k \to p$ and $w_k \to q$ are given, every sequence of complex geodesics $\varphi_k: \mathbb{D} \to \Omega$ with $z_k, w_k \in \varphi_k(\mathbb{D})$ satisfies $\varphi_k(\mathbb{D}) \cap K \neq \emptyset$ for all sufficiently large $k$.

Prove or disprove: a bounded convex domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^N$ is visible if and only if it is complex visible.
artifact.status_search_result: The equivalence is posed as a conjecture in a 2025 questions-and-conjectures paper on visibility in bounded convex domains. One direction (visibility implies complex visibility) is generally known; the converse remains unestablished, and no resolution appears in the literature found.
